subject: Post-demo follow-up: EU/APAC data boundaries & hosting recommendation
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@aurorahealth.eu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: EU/APAC data boundaries & hosting recommendation

Hi Maria — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment across Aurora's security and infra teams.

Summary of the ask
- Primary constraint: all PHI-adjacent inference must remain inside the EU (data residency requirement for processing and token storage).
- Secondary: APAC product team needs a low-latency fallback in Tokyo for regional users, but that can be async for a phase 1 launch.
- Procurement asked whether Redwood Hosted API can be configured to meet the EU-only processing constraint or if Dedicated/Private is required.

Redwood recommendation (short version)
- Hosted API with EU-only routing can meet the majority of residency controls if Aurora can accept Redwood-managed EU regions and documented cross-region failover policies (we keep compute and KV cache in EU by default).
- If Aurora requires customer-controlled networking, dedicated hardware, or in-country (Germany/Japan) on-prem processing, then Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem appliance) is the path.
- Dedicated capacity sits in the middle: predictable throughput and dedicated GPU pools in a specific region but still Redwood-managed network — good if Aurora wants isolation and throughput guarantees without on-prem ops.

Open items we need from Aurora to finalize recommendation
1) Which countries require strict in-country processing (e.g., Germany, Japan)?
2) Are there export controls for model weights or logs we need to account for?
3) Expected steady-state token volume and peak concurrency (rough ballpark is fine).

Next steps
- Please share the completed requirements_matrix.xlsx (you referenced during the call) so our solutions team can model exact hosting constraints. (Attached: sample template)
- I propose a technical deep-dive on Fri Nov 20 with our infra lead to walk residency options and failover routing — can your infra/security folks join?

Attachments: requirements_matrix.xlsx (please confirm back), SOC2 summary is available on request.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Laura from Legal for any compliance nuance and Marissa on Dedicated capacity sizing if needed.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@aurorahealth.eu>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:28:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: EU/APAC data boundaries & hosting recommendation

Thanks Sergio — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side after talking to compliance: 

1) Country-level constraints:
- Germany: Must remain in-country for any processing related to German patients (this is non-negotiable).
- Netherlands & Ireland: EU-only processing is acceptable (can live in any EU region).
- Japan: APAC users should be served locally where latency >150ms; some data must not leave Japan for 30 days.

2) Logs and token retention:
- We need an option where inference logs and prompt traces for German patients never leave Germany. Aggregated metrics are fine for EU-wide dashboards.

3) Volume:
- Expected steady-state: ~1.2M tokens/day initially; peak expected during batch jobs ~5M tokens/day (short bursts).

Given the strict Germany requirement, can Redwood Hosted API do in-country processing for Germany only, or will we need a Private deployment there? Please also advise on cross-region failover — we need assurance that in-country data will not be routed outside Germany even during decomm/failover windows.

I’ve attached the filled requirements_matrix.xlsx and SOC2 request (SOC2_summary.pdf). Happy to join a deep-dive on Nov 20 — please include your infra lead and a technical contact from our side (I’ll invite Stefan, our platform infra lead).

Best,
Maria Santos
Head of Data Engineering | Aurora Health
maria.santos@aurorahealth.eu

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: EU/APAC data boundaries & hosting recommendation

Hi Maria — looping in a short legal/controls note before the deep-dive so the infra conversation can be focused.

Key points from compliance perspective:
- In-country processing: Typically Hosted API uses regional clusters (e.g., eu-west-1, eu-central-1) and we can guarantee that processing and KV cache stay within an EU region. However, true in-country (Germany-only) requires either a Dedicated cluster deployed in the country-region or Redwood Private (VPC or an on-prem footprint) if Aurora needs exclusive control over ingress/egress rules and KMS.
- Failover behavior: Our standard hosted failover policy routes to a compatible region within the same geographic boundary (EU for EU regions). For strict in-country requirements we can enforce a no-exit policy, but that requires either Dedicated or Private so that failover targets are controlled by you rather than Redwood-managed cross-region fallback.
- Logs & retention: We can support per-customer log isolation with EU-only storage, and for German-only patient flows we recommend a Private option where the audit/log pipeline is customer-managed and can be locked to an in-country S3 equivalent or HSM-backed KMS.

I’ve attached a brief network_topology.png that shows where we can apply in-region processing and where controls tighten for in-country guarantees.

For the Nov 20 deep-dive, please have Stefan (your infra lead) available and we’ll have our infra lead (Ajay) and solutions architect (Marissa) present.

Regards,
Laura Bennett

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: EU/APAC data boundaries & hosting recommendation

Appreciate the details, Maria — that helps a lot. Quick ops notes and an ask from our side: 

- Based on your volumes (1.2M steady / 5M burst), Dedicated in eu-central-1 could satisfy throughput with reserved GPU pools and give the stronger isolation you want without full on-prem. If Germany-only processing is strict for a subset of traffic (German patients), the cleanest solution is a small Private deployment inside the country for that tenant slice, with Hosted/Dedicated for the rest.
- Action item for Aurora: can you flag whether German patient traffic is routed via a distinct customer identifier (tenant_id or workspace) in your app? If yes, we can architect a split-routing approach with prefix/KV caching scoped to the German tenant to keep that traffic in-country.
- Proposed times for the technical deep-dive (Ajay + Marissa + Stefan + Aurora infra): Nov 20 at 09:00 CET or Nov 20 at 14:00 CET — which works for you?

I’ll prepare a short runbook showing the routing approaches (hosted-eu-only, dedicated-eu, private-in-germany) with token cost/latency tradeoffs.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
